issue.title: SMAC smoother can generate infeasible paths when using non-circular robots in very confined spaces
issue.body:
Following up on https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4271#issuecomment-2879364973

The SMAC smoother could result in an infeasible (colliding) path. The reason is because after modifying the path, it does simple cell cost collision checking (rejects path if cell cost > MAX_NON_OBSTACLE) but does not check for potential collision of orientated footprints.
issue.bodyHTML:
Following up on #4271 (comment)

The SMAC smoother could result in an infeasible (colliding) path. The reason is because after modifying the path, it does simple cell cost collision checking (rejects path if cell cost > MAX_NON_OBSTACLE) but does not check for potential collision of orientated footprints.

comments.body: I want to work on this if possible. I haven't examined the code yet, but I know that there is a collision checker built into nav2. Could we potentially use that function here?
comments.bodyHTML: I want to work on this if possible. I haven't examined the code yet, but I know that there is a collision checker built into nav2. Could we potentially use that function here?

comments.body:
The issue here is that we don't have the feasibility information in the smoother currently. So, there'd have to be a check on the feasibility constraints to then be able to get the orientation information (theta) needed to check the footprint. We cannot check the footprint without X,Y,Theta for a pose since the footprint is orientation-dependent when non-circular.

So, we'd probably want to start off by estimating the orientation with the `updateApproximatePathOrientations` function to get an orientation for introducing the collision checker. Then we'd have the X,Y,Theta for each pose to use a collision checker object with (Nav2 Costmap 2D has one of these you can use, see Hybrid-A* NodeT for an example use). 

Then, perhaps trying to do one step better by either changing the way the smoother works to retain orientation information so we know its 'real' or make sure we maintain minimum turning radius constraints so that the computed orientation is known to be drivable. That way if not just collision free, but also doesn't possibly violate constraints (which is rare and not usually a big deal, but can happen and would impact vehicles like Ackermann that have an actual, strict limit)

comments.body:
Hi! I’d like to work on this issue as my first PR.

From the discussion, the main problem seems to be the lack of orientation information in the smoother’s collision check, which only uses simple cell cost and ignores the robot’s oriented footprint.

I’ve reviewed the smac_smoother.cpp code and the issue discussion, and I see that the smoother currently **only checks collisions based on cell costs from the costmap**. This approach doesn’t account for the robot’s oriented footprint, which is critical for non-circular robots in confined spaces.

To address this, I plan to: 

(Use the existing updateApproximatePathOrientations function to estimate the orientation for each pose in the smoothed path. With the (X, Y, Theta) data available, integrate Nav2’s footprint collision checker (similar to how it’s used in the Hybrid-A* planner) to validate the path.)

-> Integrate Nav2’s footprint collision checker into the smoother.

 -> After smoothing and updating the path orientations (x, y, theta), run a footprint collision check on every pose along the path.

  -> If any footprint collision is detected, reject the smoothed path and revert to the last valid path.

   -> Ensure this addition works seamlessly with the existing smoothing logic and does not degrade performance.

I’ll also add tests to verify that the smoother no longer produces infeasible paths due to footprint collisions.

I’d love to work on this as my first PR. Could I please get a go-ahead? Also, any guidance on best practices for initializing the collision checker or existing test cases to build on would be greatly appreciated!

comments.body: > Please, we'd love that! I'd say before opening a PR, keep us apprised on your progress and when you think you found the problem for us to chat about :-) Thanks! I first tried adding a regression test to show the failure mode. The test builds an unsafe path, but the smoother reports success. The strategy is not to pass an already colliding path to the smoother and expect it to fail, because that would be blending (a) upstream planner or caller giving sth invalid with (b) smoother not rejecting that invalid input, while we just want to isolate (b). So instead I tried: valid input path -> SMAC smoother changes the path -> changed path becomes colliding -> smoother still returns success Here is the added test: https://github.com/MobiusRoamer/navigation2/commit/bfb75f13 To visualize the footprint geometry a bit, `r` denotes the robot centre, ` ```text 1.2m * 0.4m [===========] [ r ] [===========] ^ center ``` X is our obstacle in the following landscape ```text y ^ | 12m r----r----r----r----r----r | | | | X obstacle around (3.1, 11.7), not to scale | | | 10m r | | | 8m r | | | 6m r | | | 4m r | | | 2m r | +--------+----+----+----+----+----+----> x 2m 4m 6m 8m 10m 12m 14m ``` See test results at end of this post. Before smoothing, every original pose is valid. I checked them using `footprint_checker.footprintCostAtPose()`. Then after smoothing, smoother moves poses between the two arms of the `L` corner, one pose gets close enough that its rectangle overlaps obstacle. The bot centre is still not on the lethal X cell, so the old centre cell check passes. But the rectangular footprint at that pose overlaps the obstacle, so the full footprint check fails. My planned fix direction is to validate the full oriented footprint during smoothing, reject an update that introduces a footprint collision, roll back to the last valid path, and return false. Does this direction match what you would expect? I'm open to changes. #### Test result To reproduce the regression test results ```bash cd git -C src/navigation2 fetch https://github.com/MobiusRoamer/navigation2.git fix/smac-smoother-footprint-5330 git -C src/navigation2 checkout FETCH_HEAD ``` then (replace `--packages-select` with `--packages-up-to nav2_smac_planner` if dependencies not installed yet) ``` colcon build \ --symlink-install \ --packages-select nav2_smac_planner \ --cmake-args -DBUILD_TESTING=ON source install/setup.bash ./build/nav2_smac_planner/test/test_smoother \ --gtest_filter='SmootherTest.rejects_non_circular_footprint_collision' ```

commit.message:
fix(smac_planner): check oriented footprint collision in smoother for non-circular robots

The SMAC path smoother was checking only the centre-point cost of each pose
after gradient descent, which allowed smoothed paths to produce lethal oriented
footprint collisions for non-circular robots (wide rectangular footprints
passing diagonally through narrow corridors pass the centre-cost check but
fail a proper footprint check).

Add an optional `footprint` parameter (default empty = circular / no change in
behaviour) to `Smoother::smooth()` and `Smoother::smoothImpl()`.  When a
footprint is provided, a `FootprintCollisionChecker` pass runs over the
smoothed path after `updateApproximatePathOrientations()`; any pose whose
oriented cost exceeds MAX_NON_OBSTACLE_COST triggers a warning and returns
false, leaving the original path unchanged.

The three planner plugins (Hybrid, 2D, Lattice) forward the costmap robot
footprint to the smoother so non-circular robots benefit automatically.

Regression test added: `test_footprint_collision_detection` sets up a corridor
with lethal walls, confirms a narrow footprint passes and a wide footprint
(1.2 m) correctly fails.

Fixes #5330

Co-Authored-By: Claude and aki1770-del <aki1770@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(smac_planner): per-iteration revert + SmoothedPathInCollision throw

Address Maurice's CHANGES_REQUESTED on PR #6081:

1. Move oriented-footprint check INTO the gradient-descent while loop
   (per r3072469939). Previously the check ran once after the loop and
   the post-loop block truncated new_path then propagated an empty path
   through the recursive smoothImpl refinement self-call, causing the
   regression test to crash on the path_size-1 underflow.

2. Per-iteration revert (path = last_path) on collision — matches the
   nav2_smoother::SimpleSmoother idiom (simple_smoother.cpp:171-178).
   Path length is preserved end-to-end. Truncation removed.

3. Throw nav2_core::SmoothedPathInCollision on oriented-footprint
   collision — matches the canonical fail-loud signal already used by
   nav2_smoother::Nav2Smoother (nav2_smoother.cpp:285-303). Caller
   receives an explicit collision exception instead of a silently
   truncated path. This closes the controller-tracking hazard for
   wide-rectangular robots in confined corridors that motivated #5330.

Test updated: wide-footprint case now expects SmoothedPathInCollision
throw and verifies path length preservation (EXPECT_EQ poses.size()).

Closes the empty-path crash that broke CI on commit 1c5feb6.
Refs #5330.

Signed-off-by: Akihiko Komada <aki1770@gmail.com>

commit.messageHeadlineHTML: fix(smac_planner): check oriented footprint collision in smoother for…
commit.messageBodyHTML: … non-circular robots The SMAC path smoother was checking only the centre-point cost of each pose after gradient descent, which allowed smoothed paths to produce lethal oriented footprint collisions for non-circular robots (wide rectangular footprints passing diagonally through narrow corridors pass the centre-cost check but fail a proper footprint check). Add an optional `footprint` parameter (default empty = circular / no change in behaviour) to `Smoother::smooth()` and `Smoother::smoothImpl()`. When a footprint is provided, a `FootprintCollisionChecker` pass runs over the smoothed path after `updateApproximatePathOrientations()`; any pose whose oriented cost exceeds MAX_NON_OBSTACLE_COST triggers a warning and returns false, leaving the original path unchanged. The three planner plugins (Hybrid, 2D, Lattice) forward the costmap robot footprint to the smoother so non-circular robots benefit automatically. Regression test added: `test_footprint_collision_detection` sets up a corridor with lethal walls, confirms a narrow footprint passes and a wide footprint (1.2 m) correctly fails. Fixes ros-navigation#5330 Co-Authored-By: Claude and aki1770-del <aki1770@gmail.com> Signed-off-by: Akihiko Komada <aki1770@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(smac_planner): per-iteration revert + SmoothedPathInCollision throw

Address Maurice's CHANGES_REQUESTED on PR #6081:

1. Move oriented-footprint check INTO the gradient-descent while loop
   (per r3072469939). Previously the check ran once after the loop and
   the post-loop block truncated new_path then propagated an empty path
   through the recursive smoothImpl refinement self-call, causing the
   regression test to crash on the path_size-1 underflow.

2. Per-iteration revert (path = last_path) on collision — matches the
   nav2_smoother::SimpleSmoother idiom (simple_smoother.cpp:171-178).
   Path length is preserved end-to-end. Truncation removed.

3. Throw nav2_core::SmoothedPathInCollision on oriented-footprint
   collision — matches the canonical fail-loud signal already used by
   nav2_smoother::Nav2Smoother (nav2_smoother.cpp:285-303). Caller
   receives an explicit collision exception instead of a silently
   truncated path. This closes the controller-tracking hazard for
   wide-rectangular robots in confined corridors that motivated #5330.

Test updated: wide-footprint case now expects SmoothedPathInCollision
throw and verifies path length preservation (EXPECT_EQ poses.size()).

Closes the empty-path crash that broke CI on commit 1c5feb6.
Refs #5330.

Signed-off-by: Akihiko Komada <aki1770@gmail.com>

I first tried adding a regression test to show the failure mode. The test builds an unsafe path, but the smoother reports success. The strategy is not to pass an already colliding path to the smoother and expect it to fail, because that would be blending (a) upstream planner or caller giving sth invalid with (b) smoother not rejecting that invalid input, while we just want to isolate (b). So instead I tried: valid input path -> SMAC smoother changes the path -> changed path becomes colliding -> smoother still returns success Here is the added test: https://github.com/MobiusRoamer/navigation2/commit/bfb75f13 To visualize the footprint geometry a bit, `r` denotes the robot centre, ` ```text 1.2m * 0.4m [===========] [ r ] [===========] ^ center ``` X is our obstacle in the following landscape ```text y ^ | 12m r----r----r----r----r----r | | | | X obstacle around (3.1, 11.7), not to scale | | | 10m r | | | 8m r | | | 6m r | | | 4m r | | | 2m r | +--------+----+----+----+----+----+----> x 2m 4m 6m 8m 10m 12m 14m ``` See test results at end of this post. Before smoothing, every original pose is valid. I checked them using `footprint_checker.footprintCostAtPose()`. Then after smoothing, smoother moves poses between the two arms of the `L` corner, one pose gets close enough that its rectangle overlaps obstacle. The bot centre is still not on the lethal X cell, so the old centre cell check passes. But the rectangular footprint at that pose overlaps the obstacle, so the full footprint check fails. My planned fix direction is to validate the full oriented footprint during smoothing, reject an update that introduces a footprint collision, roll back to the last valid path, and return false. Does this direction match what you would expect? The strategy is not to pass an already colliding path to the smoother and expect it to fail, because that would be blending (a) upstream planner or caller giving sth invalid with (b) smoother not rejecting that invalid input, while we just want to isolate (b).

So instead I tried: valid input path -> SMAC smoother changes the path -> changed path becomes colliding -> smoother still returns success
Here is the added test:
MobiusRoamer@bfb75f13

To visualize the footprint geometry a bit, r denotes the robot centre, `

        [===========]

See test results at end of this post.
Before smoothing, every original pose is valid. I checked them using footprint_checker.footprintCostAtPose().
Then after smoothing, smoother moves poses between the two arms of the L corner, one pose gets close enough that its rectangle overlaps obstacle. The bot centre is still not on the lethal X cell, so the old centre cell check passes. But the rectangular footprint at that pose overlaps the obstacle, so the full footprint check fails.

My planned fix direction is to validate the full oriented footprint during smoothing, reject an update that introduces a footprint collision, roll back to the last valid path, and return false.

Does this direction match what you would expect? I'm open to changes.

Test result

To reproduce the regression test results

cd <nav2_ws>

git -C src/navigation2 fetch https://github.com/MobiusRoamer/navigation2.git fix/smac-smoother-footprint-5330
git -C src/navigation2 checkout FETCH_HEAD

then (replace --packages-select with --packages-up-to nav2_smac_planner if dependencies not installed yet)

colcon build \
  --symlink-install \
  --packages-select nav2_smac_planner \
  --cmake-args -DBUILD_TESTING=ON

source install/setup.bash

./build/nav2_smac_planner/test/test_smoother \
  --gtest_filter='SmootherTest.rejects_non_circular_footprint_collision'
